item.title: Former King’s Lynn hospital nurse struck off
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Former King’s Lynn hospital nurse struck off
A former nurse at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has been removed from the nursing register. Adam Feary was previously convicted of possessing over 14,000 indecent images of children and animals, as well as a manual encouraging sexual offending.
The Nursing and Midwifery Council’s Fitness to Practise Committee concluded that Feary’s actions breached fundamental professional standards. While he received a suspended prison sentence last year, the committee determined that an immediate interim order was necessary to protect the public. Feary, who worked at the hospital until July 2023, has been placed on the sex offenders register for ten years. The Queen Elizabeth Hospital confirmed his employment was terminated following an internal investigation.

Rail disruption between King’s Lynn and Cambridge
Rail services between King’s Lynn and Cambridge have been cancelled following an incident where a person was struck by a train near Cambridge North. Great Northern Rail has confirmed that travel on this route is suspended until further notice while emergency services and response teams work at the scene.

Rail disruption following fatality between Ely and Cambridge North
British Transport Police have confirmed that a person has died after being struck by a train between Ely and Cambridge North stations this morning. Officers were called to the tracks at 11:16 am.
As a result, all train services between King’s Lynn and Cambridge are cancelled until further notice, affecting passengers at Watlington, Downham Market, Littleport, Ely, and Waterbeach. Great Northern Rail expects major disruption to continue until at least 6:00 pm this evening. Passengers are advised to delay travel or allow an extra hour for alternative routes. Enquiries into the circumstances of the incident are ongoing. Anyone in need of emotional support can contact Samaritans at any time by calling 116 123.

item.title: Free weekly running sessions offered at Wisbech Park
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Free weekly running sessions offered at Wisbech Park
Residents across the Fens are being invited to join a free, weekly running programme at Wisbech Park. Organised by Active Fenland, the Couch to 5k sessions take place every Tuesday morning between 9:30am and 10:30am.
The group is led by England Athletics-qualified coach Gary Bligh and is open to all abilities, regardless of previous running experience. Organisers say the sessions focus on building confidence and stamina in a supportive environment, with no pressure to meet specific pace targets. Beyond the physical exercise, the group offers a social opportunity for participants to meet new people. Those interested in taking part can simply turn up to the park to get involved.

Battle of Britain commemoration service in King’s Lynn
A wreath-laying ceremony will be held in King’s Lynn’s Tower Gardens this Monday to mark the 86th anniversary of the Battle of Britain. The service begins at 10:45am and will be led by the Reverend Canon Mark Dimond. West Norfolk Mayor, Councillor Steve Bearshaw, is expected to attend alongside representatives from the Armed Forces, local schools, and cadet groups.
The event also signals the launch of the Royal Air Forces Association’s annual Wings Appeal. Organisers are encouraging veterans and members of the public to attend the commemoration. Following the service, guests are invited to Marriotts Warehouse for refreshments.

The team is visiting all five of the charity’s hubs, including the site in Wisbech, as well as locations in Peterborough, Huntingdon, and Ely. Anglian Water crews are currently on site working to resolve the issue. The utility company expects the repairs to be completed by 1pm today. While West Norfolk Council has confirmed that local facilities remain open, commuters are advised to take care when travelling through the town centre.

item.title: Water leak causes disruption in King’s Lynn town centre
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Water leak causes disruption in King’s Lynn town centre
Drivers in King’s Lynn are facing travel disruption this morning following a water leak at the Tuesday Market Place. The leak has resulted in a large pool of water forming on the road directly outside the Alive Corn Exchange.
Engineers from Anglian Water are currently on-site carrying out repairs to address low-pressure issues in the area. West Norfolk Council has confirmed that the nearby public toilets on Ferry Street are closed while the work is underway. Motorists are advised to take care when navigating the area.
